picks.title: AI designs working molecular scissors that recognize and cut selected protein targets
picks.excerpt: Baker lab (UW) used RFdiffusion2, ProteinMPNN and AlphaFold 3 to design cysteine and zinc proteases from scratch; two Nature papers report designs that cut targets such as amyloid-beta and TDP-43, with AI refinement boosting one enzyme ~30-fold.
picks.rationale: Two Nature papers from the Baker lab: de novo AI-designed proteases that cut chosen protein targets, a new capability in enzyme design.

picks.title: Physics-guided AI reconstructs hidden patterns inside ultrathin magnets from external fields
picks.excerpt: A physics-guided neural approach infers the internal magnetization of nanoscale magnets from the stray fields microscopes can measure, solving an ill-posed inverse problem relevant to spintronic computing.
picks.rationale: Physics slot: a physics-guided neural network works out the hidden magnetization inside nanoscale magnets from the stray fields a microscope can measure, an inverse problem that matters for spintronics.

picks.title: Can AI break encryption? OpenAI's new math has cryptographers divided
picks.excerpt: OpenAI's bumper crop of 722 AI-generated math papers wowed and worried researchers, and cryptographers are split over whether the algorithms protecting texts and bank logins are next.
picks.rationale: Covers OpenAI's 722 AI-generated math papers and asks the practical question of whether encryption is next; a different event from earlier AI-math cards.

picks.title: Using electronic structure to guide AI in designing new materials
picks.excerpt: University of Tokyo researchers extended a leading generative AI materials model to condition on electronic structure, steering atom arrangements toward desired properties.
picks.rationale: Materials slot: a University of Tokyo team makes a generative materials model take electronic structure as an input, so designs can be steered toward target properties.

picks.title: He Wants AI Benchmarking To Be a Science, Not a Dark Art
picks.excerpt: Moritz Hardt, author of a new book on benchmarks, argues AI's 'standardized tests' are fundamentally broken but fixable, and lays out a science of evaluation.
picks.rationale: Methodology slot: Moritz Hardt (new book) on how to make AI evaluation a real science; different person and angle from the 10-06 benchmark-error study.
